text: The death of 8-month-old Layla Ghandour during the 2018 Gaza border protests was an international story, initially blamed on Israeli tear gas inhalation, a claim amplified by media, celebrities, and Palestinian officials. But later revelations indicated this narrative was fabricated for propaganda purposes by Hamas. A captured relative testified under Israeli interrogation that Hamas paid the family $8,000 to lie about the cause, revealing she actually died from a congenital blood disease common in the family, corroborated by an anonymous Gaza doctor's statement to the Associated Press attributing her death to a preexisting medical condition and the Gaza Health Ministry's removal of her name from the border protest's casualty list pending investigation, which they never completed.

On April 9, 1948, a fierce battle took place in the Arab village of Deir Yassin, just outside Jerusalem. For decades, it has been held up as proof of “Zionist barbarity” — the supposed deliberate massacre of 254 innocent villagers, including rapes and mutilations. The story is still repeated as gospel. Deir Yassin was a tragedy of war — a hard-fought battle in a war the Arabs launched to prevent any Jewish state from existing anywhere in the Land. It was not the deliberate ethnic cleansing or massacre of legend. The real lesson is darker: Arab leaders’ own fabricated atrocity stories caused far more Palestinian suffering than the battle itself — and they have spent decades blaming the Jews for the consequences.
